Terwilliger Center Award for Innovation in Attainable Housing 2024 Winner: 425 Grand Concourse
July 26, 2024
Share by Email.
Will open in a new window.
Share on Facebook.
Will open in a new window.
Share on X, formerly Twitter.
Will open in a new window.
Share on LinkedIn.
Will open in a new window.

Awards
Awards & Competitions
Housing
Housing - Affordable and Workforce
Jack Kemp Excellence in Affordable and Workforce Housing Award
Kemp Housing Awards
Land Use Type/Sector - Housing - Affordable/Workforce
Terwilliger Center
Terwilliger Center for Housing
425 Grand Concourse
is a 26-story, 277-unit mixed-use, mixed-income project located in the Mott Haven neighborhood of the Bronx. A premier example of sustainable design, the project currently stands as the largest Passive House-certified multifamily development in North America and will consume 70% less energy than a conventional housing project. The project units are affordable to households at a wide range of incomes (from below 30% to 130% of AMI), with 28 units designated for formerly homeless households. All 276 residential units (excluding the super’s unit) are income-restricted, with 193 units deemed permanently affordable under NYC regulatory requirements.
The project’s design and finishes showcase an attention to detail comparable to luxury market-rate developments – with resident access to a comprehensive package of amenities, including laundry facilities on every floor, bicycle storage, a fitness center, an outdoor recreation deck, outdoor rooftop garden, and community rooms. In addition to much-needed high-quality affordable housing, 425 Grand Concourse provides the community with a 29,000 square-foot City University of New York (CUNY) educational facility, a healthcare facility, a cultural space, a locally-operated supermarket, and a community comfort station.
Full case study available on ULI’s Knowledge Finder
here
.
Location:
Bronx, New York
Developers:
Trinity Financial Inc., MBD Community Housing Corporation
